newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian marines land in rebel-held Albanian city.
newsitem.headline: Italian marines land in rebel-held Albanian city.

text.p: About 150 Italian troops from a multinational security force landed by sea in the rebel-held Albanian port city of Vlore on Monday, witnesses said.

They said the heavily armed marines, the first large contingent of troops to reach Vlore since the deployment of the force began in Albania last week, disembarked in launches from the San Gusto navy ship and were busy securing the port.
The soldiers' mission will be to protect aid deliveries to the city, awash with arms since an insurrection in February.
Dozens of Italian armoured cars rolled into Vlore from the nearby city of Fier.
Last week an advance party of some two dozen Italian marines travelled to Vlore by land from the capital Tirana.
Some 750 Italian and Greek troops are expected to arrive in Vlore eventually as part of the multinational mission, Italian military sources said.

Vlore and much of southern Albania are controlled by rebel committees which reject the authority of President Sali Berisha whom they blame for the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes earlier this year.
